text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx error rate on /v1/generate (hosted-redwood-us-west). Impact: ~12% of requests failing, start=2025-11-04T02:13:20Z, severity=high. Paging on-call (priya).
Priya (on-call): I'm on it. Pulling logs + customer impact. Can someone grab which model variants are spiking errors? @Sam can you join?
Maya (sre): Noticed uptick in KV cache misses and a surge in batching queue length around 02:12 UTC in the runtime dashboards. Could be cache invalidation + batching interactions.
Sam (eng-runtime): Got the alert. Looking at traces. Seeing repeated KV cache lookup timeouts against redis-proxy and large replays for quantized-v2 models. Suspect KV cache invalidation bug after the recent warm-start change.
James (support): Affected customers: 3 mid-market customers on Dedicated (acct IDs redacted) reporting degraded tail latency and request retries. No PII leaked. Confirmed user-visible 500s for streaming endpoints.
Priya (on-call): Priorities: 1) Mitigate user impact now 2) Preserve telemetry for postmortem 3) Schedule handoff for deeper fix.
Sam (eng-runtime): For quick mitigation I can disable KV cache reads for the hosted tier and fallback to model-local KV. Rolling a config patch in 1-2 min. Command I'm about to run:
```
# toggle runtime feature flag for hosted cluster
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/featureflags \
  -d '{"feature":"kv_cache_reads","state":"off","scope":"hosted-us-west"}'
```
Priya (on-call): Do it. Also lower batching max tokens to reduce queueing pressure while we investigate: set batch_max_tokens=256 on the affected pool.
Sam (eng-runtime): Applying both now. Patch applied, rolling restart of 6/12 pods. Waiting for readiness.
ops-bot: deploy "featureflag/kv_cache_reads=off (hosted-us-west)" started by Sam — rollout 6/6 pods updated — success.
Priya (on-call): Early telemetry: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 2.1% over last 4 minutes. Tail latency improved ~40ms. Still watching.
Maya (sre): Opening an incident page: https://notion.redwood/company/incidents/INC-2025-1104-kv-batch. Adding timeline + initial hypothesis.
Liang (infra): We should consider temporarily routing traffic to non-quantized model variants for customers on Dedicated who are still seeing failures. I can add a route rule to send them to quantized-v1-stable if needed.
James (support): I've informed the customer success reps. Drafted an initial customer update: "We're mitigating a runtime caching issue impacting streaming endpoints; mitigation in progress; we'll follow up with timeline and root cause."
Priya (on-call): Handing off to Sam for long-running investigation. I'll remain as incident lead for comms. Sam, please own the post-incident action items and coordinate with Maya/Liang.
Sam (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. Initial action items I'm creating now:
- Reproduce KV cache invalidation locally with warm-start workload
- Audit recent warm-start PRs for cache lifecycle changes
- Add guardrail to prevent full-cache invalidation under high-batching pressure
- Add metric: kv_cache.invalidation_count and kv_cache.read_error_rate alert threshold
- Re-run quantization rollout canary with expanded perf checks
I'll assign owners in the postmortem doc.
Maya (sre): Please add immediate runbook updates: include an entry for "disable kv_cache_reads" and a checklist for reducing batch_max_tokens and routing to stable variants.
Sam (eng-runtime): Putting the mitigation and postmortem tracker here: https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-4876 (create if missing). Also creating PR for a quick fix: add exponential backoff to redis-proxy reads and a safety flag to prevent invalidation during warm-start.
Liang (infra): Quick routing script to send Dedicated customers on the problematic route to stable variant:
```
# temporary route rule
rbac-tool route set --customer-group dedicated-impacted --from model=quantized-v2 --to model=quantized-v1-stable --expires 2025-11-05T06:00:00Z
```
James (support): Customers notified with ETA 2 hours for full mitigation confirmation. Tickets created and linked to the incident page.
Priya (on-call): Status check at T+30m: 5xx at 1.9%, no new customer complaints. Proceed to schedule a postmortem meeting for T+48h. Sam, pick a time and invite SRE, runtime, infra, support, product.
Sam (eng-runtime): Proposed postmortem time: 2025-11-06T14:00 UTC. I'll create the calendar invite and attach the incident timeline + initial logs.
Maya (sre): Action items summary (to be added to the postmortem):
- (Sam) Root cause: investigate warm-start cache invalidation bug + batching interaction — due 2025-11-10
- (Sam) Add kv_cache.* metrics + alert — due 2025-11-07
- (Liang) Add traffic routing playbook + automated routing helper — due 2025-11-09
- (Sam/Maya) Update runbook and mitigation steps (disable kv cache, reduce batch size, route to stable) — due 2025-11-07
- (Eng Platform) Add canary checks for quantization rollouts to detect latency/error regressions earlier — owner TBD, due 2025-11-14
- (James) Customer follow-up template and post-incident notes — due 2025-11-06
Priya (on-call): I'll create a follow-up thread in #postmortems after the meeting. For now marking incident as mitigated (status: mitigated, impact: partial, scope: hosted+dedicated routing for subset). :white_check_mark:
Sam (eng-runtime): Quick note: preserving core dumps and request traces for the next 48h. If anyone needs a specific trace, ping me with trace id.
Maya (sre): Good work. We'll do a blameless postmortem. Please add logs + CI diffs to the incident doc.
James (support): I'll send the post-mitigation customer messages and close customer tickets once postmortem notes are ready.
Priya (on-call): Handing off to on-call rotation for the evening — @maya you're primary. I'll be available for comms.
Maya (sre): Acknowledged handoff. Monitoring alerts configured.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 2 hours or on request.
Sam (eng-runtime): Follow-up: I've pushed an emergency flag to prevent cache invalidation in warm-start path and a small throttle to batching. PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2345 — review appreciated.
Liang (infra): I'll own the routing playbook item. ETA looks good. Adding smoke tests to ensure route rules don't loop.
Priya (on-call): Final: postmortem invite sent, action items in JIRA, incident page updated. Great job coordinating everyone. :clap:
